source.author: Anastasia Kireeva
source.post: Low-degree hardness of finding the largest clique in Erdős–Rényi graph (problems 36-38)

methods.outcome: Exact source-flag Kato flow identified with block symmetric Toda/QR; pairwise degree bandwidth 2 is invariant; connected Taylor coefficients satisfy an explicit Catalan rooted majorant with positive system-size-independent radius.

Higher degree-gap explosion and rooted coefficient explosion are ruled out inside the explicit Catalan small-coupling region; the genuine algorithmic obstruction is quasi-local spatial QR fill-in, which requires a summable rooted norm.
All connected local graph shapes are rigorously dominated by a scalar Catalan binary-commutator-tree recursion; stars/wedges describe low orders but are not asserted globally extremal.

new_mechanism.bandwidth: Pairwise Ising source-degree bandwidth 2 is preserved exactly by the block Toda flow.
new_mechanism.rooted_majorant: h_{m+1} <= 16 sum_{p+q=m} h_p h_q, hence h_m <= C_m 16^m h_0^{m+1} and convergence for 64 h_0 |alpha| < 1.
new_mechanism.local_table_certificate: Finite star conditional tables plus the Kato/Toda majorant give an algorithmic positive tilted-coercivity interval for sufficiently weak bounded-degree zero-field pairwise Ising.

remaining_obligation: Instantiate the two-copy polymer/interface reference-pressure certificate end-to-end on the same genuinely overlapping weak-Ising or bounded-arity class.

Join local tilted transport, prior-typical reference pressure, and bounded source LDA through D=(log n)^{1+Omega(1)} in one direct local-specification theorem with explicit fixed-noise and polynomial-degree quantifiers.
Reconcile the block-Toda/Kato rooted majorant with quasi-local spectral-flow/KAM literature, especially De Roeck–Schütz, and preserve novelty discipline.
Obtain actual P26 plus one distinct OTHER full theorem/source audit before closure.
